label: Small sample
operational_paraphrase: Sample not so large that conventional rejection is obtained merely through sample size; source discusses size/power trade-off.

label: Variable description
operational_paraphrase: Units and descriptive statistics supplied for all regression variables.

label: Interpretable coefficients
operational_paraphrase: Elasticities or another economically interpretable scale allowing readers to assess impact.

label: Appropriate null
operational_paraphrase: Null corresponds to the substantive hypothesis rather than an automatic zero-null.

label: Coefficient interpretation
operational_paraphrase: Coefficients interpreted with their theoretical meaning, measurement units and data limitations in view.

label: Avoid irrelevant statistics
operational_paraphrase: Does not report all t/F statistics or standard errors indiscriminately where a test is inappropriate.

label: More than testing at first crucial use
operational_paraphrase: At the first crucial inferential passage, uses criteria of importance beyond statistical significance. Original prose question is negatively phrased; good-practice coding reverses that wording.
notes: EJW2004 comparative 1980s Q7 cell is 13.2%; original1996 table is47.3%.

label: Power mentioned
operational_paraphrase: Mentions the tests’ power, with substantive alternatives relevant to its interpretation.

label: Power acted upon
operational_paraphrase: Conditional question: if power is mentioned, takes action concerning it; source allows not-applicable for some tests.
notes: Q9 published percentage is conditional, not all-paper percentage.

label: No ranking by test statistic
operational_paraphrase: Avoids ranking coefficients by the absolute magnitude of their t statistics.

label: No sign-only interpretation
operational_paraphrase: Avoids discussing coefficient signs without discussing magnitudes.

label: Magnitude discussed
operational_paraphrase: Discusses coefficient sizes and whether corresponding variables have economic influence.

label: Substantive comparison
operational_paraphrase: Places large/small coefficient judgments in a scientific conversation about relevant quantitative comparisons.

label: Variable selection
operational_paraphrase: Avoids choosing variables for inclusion solely by statistical significance.
notes: Q14 and Q15 printed percentages are transposed relative to supplied matrix labels.

label: After the crucial passage
operational_paraphrase: Uses criteria of importance beyond statistical significance after the principal test.
notes: Q14 and Q15 printed percentages are transposed relative to supplied matrix labels.

label: Testing not decisive alone
operational_paraphrase: Does not let statistical significance end the empirical argument. Original prose question asks whether it is decisive; good-practice coding reverses that wording.

label: Reasonableness calculation
operational_paraphrase: Uses simulation to examine whether coefficients are reasonable, beyond merely inserting regressions in a further argument; excludes screening simulation inputs only by statistical significance.

label: Distinguish in conclusions
operational_paraphrase: Keeps statistical significance distinct from economic, policy and scientific importance in conclusions and implications.

label: Unambiguous significance
operational_paraphrase: Avoids switching between statistical and substantive meanings of significance without distinction.
